plugins.name: Fetchify
plugins.author: Fetchify
plugins.short_description: This plugin adds global address auto-complete functionality to the address forms on the front-end in WooCommerce.
plugins.description:
This plugin can be configured to provide up to 4 different data validation products. It replaces our previous plugins Crafty Clicks Address Auto-Complete and Crafty Clicks Postcode Lookup.

Address Auto-Complete

Adds address auto-fill, lookup and validation to address forms on the front-end in WooCommerce for over 240 countries.

The checkout experience becomes faster and easier as a customer no longer has to type out their full address. The smart predictive search helps speed up form filling and boosts usability. Every address is verified at the point of entry. Problems due to incorrect or badly typed address data are drastically reduced.

Postcode Lookup

The defacto solution for address capture and validation in the UK. Enter any UK postcode in the search field, click the search button and the drop down will show all the relevant address results for that postcode. Select the required address and the form will immediately be populated with accurate information.

Phone Validation

Verifies all number types and formats including mobile, international and landline numbers in every country/territory worldwide. Corrects and re-formats common mistakes within forms to ensure data quality.

Email Validation

Email Validation provides real-time validation of any email address. Invalid format emails are declined immediately while valid emails are checked to ensure they link to an active provider. The API verifies username and domain elements of the email address.

Customer Satisfaction & Conversions

Easier and faster checkout saves your customers’ time, improves conversions and builds loyalty.

Data Quality

User input is validated in real time and your customer database is populated with fully verified addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. Address verification can reduce failed deliveries by up to 50%.

WPML Compatibility

This plugin is compatible with WPML to make your checkout multilingual. To find out more about WPML go to https://wpml.org/

Getting Started

In order to use this service, you will need to sign up for an account. You will then receive an access token which will give you access to our service. You need to insert this access token in the configuration options. We offer 30 free searches for testing purposes, but in order to use this plugin on a live site, you must have a paid account with us.

Automatic Updates

Our service is split into 3 parts:

  1. An API server that delivers the data
  2. A JS library that can retrieve the data, and generate a basic UI, regardless of platform
  3. WooCommerce specific JS files (located in clicktoaddress-auto-complete/frontend/js and clicktoaddress-auto-complete/admin/js)

The JS library is located on our CDN to ensure that you will automatically receive any updates. If there’s an update to the API and changes to the JS library are required in order for the plugin to function correctly, you will not have to worry about updating it yourself.

Every autofilled postal code was verified against Sri Lanka Post and independent directories (July 2026). Cities whose codes could not be fully verified are left out — for those, the city field simply works as a plain text box.

  • WooCommerceの購入手続き、カート、マイアカウントの住所フォームに対応します。
  • WooCommerce Blocksの購入手続き・カート住所フィールド更新に対応します。
  • 郵便番号から都道府県・市区町村・町域の入力を補助します。
  • 通常の住所検索にはローカル郵便番号データベースを使用します。

  • 管理者が郵便番号データベース更新を手動実行した場合だけ、日本郵便の公式郵便番号CSVを取得します。

  • ローカル郵便番号データベースを使って、郵便番号と都道府県・市区町村の一致を確認します。
  • クラシック購入手続きとCheckout Block／Store API注文の両方でサーバー側検証を行います。

External Services

このプラグインは、管理者が設定画面で郵便番号データベースの更新ボタンを押した場合だけ、日本郵便から郵便番号CSVを取得できます。

外部サービスの利用目的

送信される情報とタイミング

  • 住所検索時に、お客様の住所、購入手続き情報、個人情報を日本郵便へ送信しません。
  • お客様の購入手続きや住所入力時には、日本郵便や外部サービスへ接続しません。

サービス提供元

  • 日本郵便
  • サービス情報: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/service/search/zipcode/download/utf-zip.html
  • 利用条件: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/
  • プライバシーポリシー: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/privacy.html

お客様の住所検索には、WordPress内に保存されたローカル郵便番号データベースを使用します。

  • PHP 7.4以上
  • WooCommerce

Enter addresses twice as fast and naturally improve checkout completion!

plugins.description:
GeoScale adds address autocomplete to WooCommerce checkout, helping customers enter addresses faster and reducing
address errors.

As a customer types a billing or shipping address, GeoScale provides matching suggestions. Selecting a suggestion
automatically fills the relevant WooCommerce address fields.

GeoScale currently supports:

  • Netherlands
  • Belgium
  • Luxembourg
  • Germany
  • Austria
  • Switzerland
  • France

The plugin works with both the WooCommerce Checkout Block and classic shortcode checkout.

A GeoScale account with an active subscription and API key is required. The plugin is open source, while the GeoScale
Address API is a separate usage-based paid service.

For pricing and more information, visit GeoScale.

External Services

This plugin connects to the GeoScale Address API at api.geoscale.io to provide address autocomplete.

When a customer uses address autocomplete during WooCommerce checkout, the plugin sends the following information to

  • Address search text entered by the customer
  • Selected checkout country
  • Customer’s browser language
  • GeoScale address identifier when a suggestion is selected

The store’s GeoScale API key is sent with API requests for authentication. The API key is transmitted server-to-server
and is not exposed to the customer’s browser.

This information is sent only when address autocomplete is used and is necessary to provide address suggestions and
retrieve selected addresses.

GeoScale: https://www.geoscale.io/

plugins.name: Moradas — Portuguese Address Autocomplete for WooCommerce
plugins.author: moradasdev
plugins.short_description: Address autocomplete for Portugal in the WooCommerce checkout: street, locality and the exact seven-digit postal code (CP7). Free, no API key.
plugins.description:
Customers type their address once, in one line, and pick it from a list. The
plugin fills in the street, the postal locality and the exact seven-digit
Portuguese postal code (código postal, CP7): the code carriers need on the
shipping label, chosen by door number. Moradas is Portuguese for “addresses”.

It is built for stores that ship to Portugal. Missing accents, abbreviations and
small typos are understood (“av liberdade lisboa 196” becomes Avenida da
Liberdade, Lisboa, 1250-147), and a postal code typed on its own fills in the
street and the locality. The service behind the plugin is free and public: no
API key, no account, and the typed text is not stored.

How it works

  1. The customer starts typing in the address field of the checkout: street,
    locality and door number, all in one line.
  2. Suggestions appear under the field as they type, each with its postal code.
    When a street has several postal codes and the door number is still missing,
    the suggestion says so.
  3. The customer picks one. Street, locality and postal code are filled in, and
    every field stays editable.

What you get in the checkout

  • One line is enough: “av liberdade lisboa 196” resolves to Avenida da Liberdade, Lisboa, 1250-147.
  • The exact CP7 for the door number, not just a code for the street or the town.
  • A postal code works as input too: “1000-098” fills in Praça do Chile, Lisboa.
  • Forgiving matching: accents are optional (“sao joao”), abbreviations are understood (“av” for Avenida), small typos are corrected.
  • Larger towns are ranked first.
  • Suggestions only for Portugal: for any other country the checkout is untouched.
  • On WooCommerce 9.9 and newer the suggestion list is drawn by WooCommerce itself, so it follows your theme.
  • Nothing is added to the order and no extra fields are created: the plugin fills the standard address, city and postcode fields.

Privacy

  • No cookies, no tracking, no account.
  • While the customer types in the address field, the typed text is sent to the Moradas service at moradas.dev to produce the suggestions (see “External services” below). Nothing is sent from any other page, from the WordPress admin, or when the plugin is activated.
  • No name, e-mail, phone number, order or account data is sent.
  • The service does not store the typed text; it keeps only hourly aggregate usage counts.
  • The bundled widget can report errors to the service; in this plugin that option is switched off.

Compatibility

  • Both checkouts: the Checkout Blocks (the default checkout) and the classic shortcode checkout. The plugin registers itself as a WooCommerce address autocomplete provider, so the same suggestions appear in both.
  • WordPress 6.5 or newer, PHP 7.4 or newer. WooCommerce 9.9 or newer for the block checkout (tested up to 11.2); with older WooCommerce versions the plugin still works in the classic checkout, using its own suggestion list.
  • Declares compatibility with High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and with the Cart and Checkout blocks.

Free, no API key

The service at https://moradas.dev is public and free, including for commercial
use. There is no key to paste and no account to create. Fair-use limits are
described at https://moradas.dev/docs. Stores that run their own instance of the
service can point the plugin to it under WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → Moradas.

Portuguese translation included

The plugin’s interface text (the settings, the admin notices and the “enter the
door number” hint in the checkout) ships with a Portuguese (Portugal)
translation. The suggestions themselves are addresses, so they read the same in
any language.

External services

This plugin connects to the Moradas address API (https://moradas.dev), a free
public service run by the authors of this plugin, to turn what the customer types
into address suggestions and into the exact postal code. Without this service the
plugin has nothing to suggest.

When it is used: only on the checkout page and only when the country is Portugal,
while the customer types in the address field, and once more when a suggestion is
picked. Nothing is sent when the plugin is activated, in the WordPress admin, or
on any other page.

What is sent: the text typed in the address field (for example
“av liberdade lisboa 196”) and, when a postal code has to be resolved, the
identifier of the chosen street together with the door number. No name, e-mail,
phone number, order or account data is sent. The requests go from the customer’s
browser straight to the API, without cookies; like any web request, they include
the browser’s IP address and user agent. The service does not store the typed
text and keeps only hourly aggregate usage counts.

Terms of use and usage limits: https://moradas.dev/docs
Privacy policy: https://moradas.dev/privacy

plugins.name: NACSTech Estimated Delivery Dates for WooCommerce
plugins.author: nacstech
plugins.short_description: Show customers exactly when their order will arrive, right on the product, cart, and checkout pages, with category, shipping-class, variation, shippin …
plugins.description:
NACSTech Estimated Delivery Dates for WooCommerce tells customers how many days their order will take to arrive, right on the product page, cart, and checkout (classic and block-based). You don’t have to set a delivery date on every product one by one — set a default once, then override it by category, shipping class, product, variation, shipping zone, or specific postcode only where you need to.

Key features

  • Global default delivery day range (storewide)
  • Per-category override
  • Per-shipping-class override
  • Per-product override
  • Per-variation override, for variable products
  • Per shipping-zone override
  • Per-postcode/zip code override, with CSV bulk import/export
  • Restrict payment methods (e.g. disable Cash on Delivery) per postcode
  • Fully block checkout for postcodes you do not deliver to
  • Order cut-off time (orders placed after this time count from the next business day)
  • Configurable business days (exclude weekends)
  • Holiday exclusion list
  • Works on classic and WooCommerce Blocks cart/checkout
  • Live “order within Xh Ym for same-day dispatch” countdown to today’s cut-off time
  • Customizable date format, message templates, and box colors, translatable via WPML/Polylang
  • Admin Delivery Simulator to test rules without placing a real order
  • [nacs_edd_estimate] shortcode to show the estimate anywhere
  • Estimate is saved on the order and shown in order emails, the thank-you page, My Account, and the admin order screen

Recommended setup

  1. Go to WooCommerce > Estimated Delivery.
  2. Set a global min/max delivery day range and cut-off time.
  3. Add category, shipping-class, product, or variation-level overrides where needed.
  4. Add shipping-zone overrides for zones that ship faster or slower than the default.
  5. Add postcode rules for exceptions: faster/slower postcodes, payment-method restrictions, or areas you don’t deliver to at all.
  6. Choose where the estimate should be displayed (product page, cart, checkout), and optionally enable the same-day dispatch countdown.

External services

This plugin can connect to an external service in the following case:

  1. Deactivation feedback email to NACSTech

When the plugin is deactivated, the plugins screen can show an optional feedback form. If the admin chooses “Submit & Deactivate”, the plugin sends a feedback email to NACSTech.

What the service is used for:
To collect optional product feedback and troubleshooting context when a site admin deactivates the plugin.

What data is sent and when:
The feedback request is sent only when the admin manually chooses “Submit & Deactivate” in the deactivation feedback form. It sends the selected reason, optional details entered by the admin, site name, site URL, admin email, WordPress version, and WooCommerce version to NACSTech support using your site’s WordPress mail configuration.

Service provider:
NACSTech

Links: Support page | Terms of service | Privacy policy

plugins.name: Hera Japan Postcode Autofill for WooCommerce
plugins.author: HeraPress
plugins.short_description: Fill in a Japanese address from its postcode at WooCommerce checkout, with Japan Post data that ships with the plugin. No API key, no external calls.
plugins.description:
Hera Japan Postcode Autofill for WooCommerce fills in the prefecture, city and street of a Japanese address as soon as the customer types the 7-digit postcode. It works on the Checkout block, on the classic checkout and on the address form under My account, for billing and shipping addresses alike.

This is an independent plugin, not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by WooCommerce or Automattic. WooCommerce is a trademark of Automattic Inc.

When the country of an address is Japan, WooCommerce already asks for the postcode before the prefecture, city and street. A Japanese postcode settles most of what comes after it, so the customer types seven digits and checks the result instead of typing the address out. The plugin works for any store that ships to Japan, whatever language the store itself uses.

Features

  • The prefecture (WooCommerce’s state field), the city and the street are filled in as soon as the seventh digit is typed.
  • Works with the Checkout block, the classic checkout and My account > Addresses.
  • Never overwrites a street the customer typed. When the postcode changes, the prefecture and city follow it, and what the plugin filled in is cleared again if the postcode is no longer complete.
  • Accepts full-width digits such as １００－０００１ and rewrites them as 100-0001, the form WooCommerce accepts, as soon as all seven are in.
  • Fills in only what the postcode settles. A postcode shared by several towns leaves the street empty, and one shared by two cities leaves the city empty, instead of guessing.
  • Covers about 143,000 postcodes, including those Japan Post assigns to a single large business, which fill in the street number as well.
  • Acts only on addresses whose country is Japan. Addresses in other countries work as before.
  • Tells screen reader users when it has filled in an address.
  • Nothing to configure: no settings screen and no database tables.

No external connections

The postcode data ships inside the plugin, in one small file for each set of first three digits. When a customer types a postcode, the browser loads that one file from your own site. Nothing is sent to Japan Post or to any other service, no remote script is loaded, and the plugin stores nothing.

Postcode data

The data comes from the postcode files Japan Post publishes for addresses and for large businesses, in the release of 30 September 2026. Japan Post states that it does not claim copyright on this data and that anyone may redistribute it: https://www.post.japanpost.jp/service/search/zipcode/download/utf-readme.html. Plugin updates bring newer data, and the changelog names the release each version carries.

Documentation

The user guide is at herapress.com/docs.

Support

Use the support forum on this plugin’s WordPress.org page. Please say which postcode you typed, whether your store uses the Checkout block or the classic checkout, and which WordPress and WooCommerce versions it runs.

plugins.name: Adeniyikayode Nigerian Postcode for WooCommerce
plugins.author: Kayode Adeniyi
plugins.short_description: Nigeria's NIPOST digital postcode at checkout: checked, tidied, found from the customer's location, and usable in shipping zones.
plugins.description:
Nigeria’s National Digital Alphanumeric Postcode System (NDAPS) gives every building an 11-character code such as EK-01-A03-FK-01: state, LGA, district, area, and building unit. It is Nigeria’s new postal code, or zip code.

This plugin does not add a field. It teaches WooCommerce’s own postcode field about Nigerian codes, so the postcode reaches everything that already reads that field: orders, emails, exports, the REST API, couriers, and shipping zones.

  • Shows the field. WooCommerce hides the postcode for Nigerian addresses. The plugin shows it and keeps it optional.
  • Checks the code. A code with the wrong shape is refused, in both the classic and the block checkout.
  • Tidies the code. ek 01 a03 fk 01 and EK01A03FK01 are both stored as EK-01-A03-FK-01.
  • Works with shipping zones. Add a postcode rule such as EK-01* to a zone to price delivery for one LGA.
  • Find my postcode. A button fills the field from the customer’s location, and asks them to confirm it.
  • Check orders. After each order, a note says whether NIPOST has a building for the postcode.

The first four need no account or key. The last two need a key from the NIPOST developer dashboard.

This is an independent project. It is not made or endorsed by NIPOST or by WooCommerce.

External services

This plugin connects to the NIPOST Postcode API at api.postcode.gov.ng, and only after you enter an API key in its settings.

  • When a customer presses “Find my postcode”, the latitude and longitude from their browser are sent, with your key, to find the nearest building. The plugin does not store or log the location.
  • After an order is placed, if “Check orders” is on, the order’s postcode is sent, with your key, to ask whether it belongs to a building. Nothing else about the order or the customer is sent.

The service is provided by the Nigerian Postal Service: terms and privacy policy.

PostcodeEU
PostcodeAPI
Pro6PP
Nederland Postcode
Postcode Connect

External services
